name: From Harappa to Freedom: The Story of India
description: Cities, scriptures, emperors and prophets of the subcontinent, from the Indus valley through the Mughals and the Raj to independence.

checkpoints.name: Indus cities and Vedic hymns
checkpoints.note: Cities like Mohenjo-daro used a script no one can read yet. The Rigveda and later epics such as the Mahabharata and Ramayana were composed, and the Buddha and Mahavira taught new paths.

checkpoints.name: Mauryas and Guptas
checkpoints.note: Ashoka, of the Maurya Empire, carved his edicts on pillars, and the Arthashastra set out statecraft. Under the Gupta Empire came the mathematics of Aryabhata and the learning of Nalanda.

checkpoints.name: Sultans, kingdoms and saints
checkpoints.note: Chess took shape as chaturanga around 600. Later the Delhi Sultanate ruled in the north while Vijayanagara flourished in the south, with its capital at Hampi, and Guru Nanak began the Sikh faith, whose teachings spread in Punjab.

checkpoints.name: The Mughal age
checkpoints.note: Akbar built a tolerant empire and the Mughals raised the Taj Mahal. Sikhs completed the Golden Temple at Amritsar, while the English East India Company arrived to trade on the coasts.

checkpoints.name: Company rule and the Raj
checkpoints.note: Victory at Plassey began the Company's rule. After the 1857 rebellion the British Raj began, Congress and Tagore gave India a voice, and Gandhi led the Salt March in 1930.

checkpoints.name: Freedom and partition
checkpoints.note: India became free in 1947, but partition split the land. Nehru was the first prime minister, the Bengal famine had shown the cost of the old rule, and a new constitution came in 1949.
